units.title: Love
units.intro: Grammar: linking words that join ideas: and, but, or (conjunctions) and however, moreover, therefore/hence (adverbials).

cards.title: Linking words
rule: **and** adds, **but** contrasts, **or** gives a choice; they join words or clauses inside one sentence: *I love my country **and** I want to serve it.*
**Moreover** (addition), **however** (contrast), **therefore / hence** (result) usually start a new sentence or clause and are followed by a comma: *He was tired. **However**, he kept working.*

examples.text: He studied hard. Therefore, he passed.
He was ill, however he came.
examples.fix: He was ill; however, he came.

cards.title: Forms and examples
head: Linker
Meaning
Example
rows: It was late but we stayed.
It is cheap. Moreover, it is useful.
It rained. However, we went out.
He trained daily. Therefore, he won.

cards.title: Common mistakes
head: Wrong
Right
Why
rows: He was tired, but however he worked.
He was tired, but he worked.
It was cheap. Moreover it is old.
It was cheap. However, it was old.
Moreover adds a similar idea; for contrast use however.
Therefore needs a cause before it.

cards.title: Memory tip
body: Think **A-C-R**: Addition (and, moreover), Contrast (but, however), Result (therefore, hence).

cards.title: Unit summary
body: And/but/or join ideas inside one sentence. Moreover (addition), however (contrast) and therefore/hence (result) link sentences and take a comma after them.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: Since the local library was renovated last year, the number of visitors ________ significantly.

steps.text: The subject is 'the number of visitors' (singular).
The sentence describes an action that started in the past (renovated last year) and continues to have relevance in the present, requiring the present perfect tense ($$\text{has/have} + \text{V}_3$$).
Students often see 'visitors' (plural) and choose 'have increased' (Option B).

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: The science teacher asked Dawit, 'Why ________ your assignment on time yesterday?'

steps.text: This is a direct question in the past simple tense.
Option A incorrectly combines 'didn't' with the past tense verb 'completed'.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The rare African manuscript ________ from the national archives before the guards noticed the broken window.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The sentence describes two past events: the manuscript being stolen and the guards noticing the broken window. The theft happened before the guards noticed it, requiring the past perfect passive voice ($$\text{had been} + \text{V}_3$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Option A ('was stolen') is simple past passive. While grammatically correct in isolation, it does not correctly sequence the two past actions. Option D ('has been stolen') is present perfect, which cannot be paired with the simple past past clause ('before the guards noticed').

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
እዚ ምሉእ ሓሳብ ክልተ ኣብ ሕሉፍ ግዜ ዝተፈጸሙ ድርጊታት የነጻጽር። እቲ ጽሑፍ ዝተሰረቐሉ ግዜ፡ እቶም ሓለውቲ ቅድሚ ምርኣዮም ስለ ዝኾነ፡ ካብቲ ሓደ ሕሉፍ ግዜ ንላዕሊ ዝቐደመ (earlier past) እዩ። ስለዚ ሕሉፍ ፍጹም ጥንሳዊ መዋቕር (past perfect passive) 'had been stolen' (Option B) ክንጥቀም ኣለና።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Each of the candidates who applied for the engineering position ________ a written test.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The subject of the sentence is 'Each' (singular), which always takes a singular verb and auxiliary ($$\text{Each} \rightarrow \text{singular verb}$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often look at the plural noun closest to the verb ('candidates') and incorrectly select the plural auxiliary 'have' (Option B) or 'are' (Option C). This is a classic subject-verb agreement trap.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
እቲ ዋና ባእታ 'Each' (ነፍሲ ወከፍ) ስለ ዝኾነ፡ ብሰዋስው ወግዒ ነጸላ (singular) እዩ። ስለዚ ምስኡ ዝኸይድ ነጸላ ግሲ 'has to take' (Option A) ክኸውን ኣለዎ። 'candidates' (ሕጹያት) ዝብል ቃል ብዙሕ ስለ ዝኾነ 'have' ምምራጽ ጌጋ እዩ።

glossary.meaning: A word that joins words or clauses: and, but, or.
A word like however or therefore that links sentences.

tips.text: Think **A-C-R**: Addition (and, moreover), Contrast (but, however), Result (therefore, hence).

games.title: Match the form to its example

questions.q: The road was dangerous. ____, they continued their journey.
questions.label: 1. The road was dangerous. ____, they continued their journey.

similar.q: Join with however: It was expensive. We bought it.
similar.a: It was expensive. However, we bought it.

similar.q: Choose: He is kind (and / but) generous.
similar.a: and. Both are positive qualities: addition.

why: Continuing despite danger is a contrast.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: She studied every day; ____, she passed with high marks.
questions.label: 2. She studied every day; ____, she passed with high marks.

similar.q: Choose: He is kind (and / but) generous.
similar.a: and. Both are positive qualities: addition.

similar.q: Join with therefore: The bus was late. We missed the class.
similar.a: The bus was late; therefore, we missed the class.

why: Passing is the result of studying.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: You can pay now ____ next week.
questions.label: 3. You can pay now ____ next week.

In addition / also. It adds another similar point.

questions.q: The house is big. ____, it has a lovely garden.
questions.label: 4. The house is big. ____, it has a lovely garden.

similar.a: In addition / also. It adds another similar point.

similar.q: Join with however: It was expensive. We bought it.
similar.a: It was expensive. However, we bought it.

why: The second sentence adds another good point.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: He loves animals ____ he looks after a dog and two cats.
questions.label: 5. He loves animals ____ he looks after a dog and two cats.

questions.label: 6. I wanted to come, ____ I was busy.

similar.q: Choose: He is kind (and / but) generous.
similar.a: and. Both are positive qualities: addition.

why: Wanting vs. being busy is a contrast inside one sentence.
